items.tr: "Zvaty" fiilinden önce kişi accusative halde gelir (мене), isim ise nominatif kalır — "ben" öznesiyle çekim yapılmaz.
items.en: "Мене звати" literally means "[they] call me" — the pronoun is accusative (мене) and the name stays nominative; don't conjugate with "я".
items.context: Мене звати Оксана. / ✗ Я звати Оксана.

items.en: You want to know where they are from.
They ask where you are from.
You ask how they are doing.

items.tr: Ukraynaca birine doğrudan seslenirken hâlâ kullanılan vocative (seslenme) hali gerekir — nominatif değil.
items.en: Ukrainian actively uses the vocative case when addressing someone directly — "продавець" (seller) becomes "продавче" in direct address, not the nominative form.
items.context: Продавче, скільки це коштує? / ✗ Продавець, скільки це коштує?

items.en: You see a jacket you like.

items.context: Продавче, у вас є інший розмір?

items.en: You are at the fruit stand.
You decide to buy the cheaper one.

items.target: Продавче, у вас є інший розмір?
items.tr: Satıcı bey, bunun başka bedeni var mı?
items.en: Sir, do you have this in another size?

items.tr: "Saat X'te" derken "o" edatı + saat sayısının lokatif hali kullanılır: "о сьомій" ("yedide"), "в сім" değil.
items.en: "At X o'clock" uses the preposition "о" + the ordinal hour number in the locative case ("о сьомій годині"), not "в" + the cardinal number.
items.context: Зустрінемось о сьомій годині. / ✗ Зустрінемось в сім годині.
Мій номер телефону: дев'ять, нуль, один.

items.en: They ask when the shop closes.

items.target: Мій номер телефону: дев'ять, нуль, один.
items.en: My phone number is nine, zero, one.
The store is open until eight.

items.tr: İyelik zamiri "mіy/moya/moye" ismin cinsiyetine göre değişir, sahibinin cinsiyetine göre değil.
items.en: The possessive "мій/моя/моє" agrees with the gender of the noun it modifies, not the owner's gender — сестра is feminine, so it's "моя сестра", never "мій сестра".
items.context: Це моя сестра. / ✗ Це мій сестра.

items.en: They ask where your parents live.
items.context: Мої батьки живуть в іншому місті.
Скільки у тебе братів і сестер?

items.en: They ask about your spouse's job.

items.target: Мої батьки живуть в іншому місті.
items.en: My parents live in another city.

items.target: Скільки у тебе братів і сестер?
items.en: How many siblings do you have?
My wife works as a doctor.

items.tr: Ukraynacada hava durumu kişisiz kurulur: fiil kullanılmadan sadece zarf (холодно, тепло) kullanılır.
items.en: Weather is expressed impersonally in Ukrainian — just the adverb form (холодно, тепло), with no "to be" verb in the present tense.
You hear drops on the roof.
You warn a friend before they leave.
A tourist asks about summer here.
It's very hot here in summer.

items.tr: Bir araçla gitmek için "їхати" fiili kullanılır; "іти" sadece yürüyerek gitmek içindir.
items.en: For traveling by vehicle use "їхати" — "іти" is only for going on foot.
items.context: Я їду на автобусі. / ✗ Я йду на автобусі.

items.en: You are at the ticket window.
items.context: Один квиток до вокзалу, будь ласка.

items.en: You're unsure which bus to take.
You're not sure where to get off.
How do I get to the city center?
Where is the nearest metro station?

items.target: Один квиток до вокзалу, будь ласка.
items.en: One ticket to the station, please.
Does this bus go to the airport?
Should I get off at the next stop?

items.tr: "İhtiyacım var" derken kişi datif halde olur (мені), ihtiyaç duyulan şey "потрібен/потрібна/потрібне" ile cinsiyetine göre uyum sağlar.
items.en: "To need" uses the dative person (мені) + "потрібен/потрібна/потрібне" agreeing with the gender of the thing needed — the person is never the nominative subject.
items.context: Мені потрібна допомога! / ✗ Я потрібна допомога!

items.en: A stranger stops to check on you.
You check your bag and panic.
You need to report a theft.

items.tr: Günlük rutin fiillerinin çoğu Ukraynacada "-ся" ekiyle dönüşlüdür (прокидатися) — Türkçedeki karşılığı dönüşlü olmasa bile.
items.en: Many daily-routine verbs are reflexive in Ukrainian, ending in "-ся" (прокидатися "to wake up"), even when the English equivalent isn't reflexive.
items.context: Я прокидаюся о сьомій. / ✗ Я прокидаю о сьомій.

items.en: I wash up and have breakfast.
I go to bed at eleven.

items.tr: Geçmiş zaman fiili öznenin cinsiyetine göre çekimlenir: erkek özne "-в" (пішов), kadın özne "-ла" (пішла).
items.en: Ukrainian past-tense verbs agree with the subject's grammatical gender — masculine subjects take "-в" (пішов), feminine subjects take "-ла" (пішла).
items.context: Вчора вона пішла в кіно. / ✗ Вчора вона пішов в кіно.
